discovery: Electron spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots: proposal and realization of quantum computing with single spins

nominees.name: David P. DiVincenzo
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich and RWTH Aachen University, Germany

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Kavli Institute of Nanoscience, Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum information in semiconductors
motivation: In 1998 Loss and DiVincenzo showed that the spin of a single electron confined in a semiconductor quantum dot could serve as a qubit, with exchange-based two-qubit gates controlled by electrostatic gates. DiVincenzo's criteria became the framework against which every quantum-computing platform is judged. Vandersypen and colleagues turned the proposal into physics: single-shot readout of an individual electron spin, coherent single-spin control by electric-dipole spin resonance, and, more recently, high-fidelity universal gates and multi-qubit processors in silicon and germanium. Together these works established that quantum coherence of a single spin can be initialised, controlled, entangled and read out inside a solid-state transistor-like device. That has created a scalable route to quantum processors that is compatible with semiconductor manufacturing. The field now spans many laboratories and foundries worldwide, and it shows how a fundamental idea, pursued with precision, becomes technology.
